comment: Phase 8 (APR-JE-036): the extraction and migration matrix. An ASSESSMENT: nothing here extracts, copies or implements framework code, and the framework repository is not modified. Target locations are architectural recommendations, not facts. check:framework-matrix proves that every file of the repository belongs to exactly one component and that every reference resolves; engineering/FRAMEWORK-MIGRATION-MATRIX.md is generated from this file.

frameworkReference.architectureSpecs: 01 to 15, byte-identical at both commits (blob hashes compared)

classes.universal: Reusable across all STS client websites with parameterisation only (values move to the project manifest; logic is unchanged).
classes.universal-redesign: Reusable only after a design change (a mechanism that encodes a Jade & Ember assumption, or a finding from Phases 5 to 7).
classes.adapter-industry: Belongs to one industry (restaurant) and stays with projects of that industry.
classes.adapter-hosting: Belongs to one hosting provider or delivery mode.
classes.project: A fact about Jade & Ember or its delivered site; stays.
classes.devtool: Development and test tooling; kept optional, never a release dependency.
classes.record: Project history, decisions and evidence; stays.
classes.doc: Documentation that is rewritten into the framework specification.

components.name: Core utilities
components.summary: Repository paths, git helpers, JSON-Schema subset validator, HTML tokenizer, media header readers, flash proxy, screenshot comparison, ZIP reader/writer, known-findings register mechanism.

redesign.notes: git.mjs fixes the layout <repo>/jade-and-ember/engineering, the docs path and the v0.8 baseline export; these become values read from the project manifest (sts.engineering.json). The other modules are already free of project names.

components.verify: Unit cases against the generic fixture site; ZIP round trip; schema validator conformance cases; the same 38-check result on Jade & Ember before and after (parity).

components.name: Site assembly and byte-immutability rules
components.summary: assembleCandidate (fresh build into a temp folder), the page registry reader (pagesOf), the SHARED file list, and the immutability allowlist validator that reads the approvals log.

redesign.notes: Splits into generic assembly (page registry, shared and asset folders from the manifest) and the baseline immutability rules (FM-06). SHARED = styles.css, site.js, hero.js, menu.js is Jade-specific; the allowlist validator names docs/JADE_AND_EMBER_APPROVALS.md.

components.verify: Assemble the generic fixture, Jade & Ember and the cinematic template (single page) with identical code paths; byte-identical Jade & Ember output before and after.

components.name: Verify runner and report
components.summary: npm run verify: ordered checks, one summary, exit code, and the .reports/verify.json report (mode, commit, dirty, assetsTree) the release gate reads.

redesign.notes: The check list is 38 hard-coded imports and registrations; it becomes a registry (framework checks plus project checks) selected by the manifest. The report is the evidence the release gate trusts (finding RG-08): it must become authentic and bound to the candidate artifact digest.

components.verify: Runs the generic fixture and Jade & Ember with the same runner; the report is rejected when forged or incomplete (Gate 6 dry-run scenarios).

components.name: Browser runtime, test server and engine data
components.summary: Pinned browser launch (CHROMIUM_PATH), the shared browser-check runtime, the configurable static test server that models host behaviours, engine console-noise filters, the environment pin.

redesign.notes: engine-noise.mjs holds the Firefox hero-video preload message (a Jade & Ember fact) and environment.json pins Chromium 141 and tolerances; both become project/framework data. server.mjs host profiles move to the hosting adapters (FM-22).

components.verify: Fixture runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; noise filters are scoped per engine and per project; version pins are read from data.

components.name: Cross-browser harness
components.summary: Runs the browser checks in Chromium, Firefox or WebKit and prints a matrix in which no check can be silently left out.

redesign.notes: The catalogue classifies Jade & Ember's 38 checks by name; classification must come from each check's own declaration so a project check cannot be unclassified (selftest-gate5 refused one in Phase 7).

components.verify: selftest-gate5 equivalent on the fixture: an unclassified or skipped check is shown as MISSING, never as a pass.

components.name: Baseline immutability and regression mechanism
components.summary: Compares a candidate with a frozen approved reference (git commit) at byte, text, structure, computed-style, pixel and behaviour level, with an owner-approved difference allowlist.

redesign.notes: A new client has no v0.8. The baseline must become an optional, project-declared approved reference (for example the first owner-approved release), with the approval ids and the allowlist format parameterised. Scenarios (FM-12) are project code.

components.verify: On the fixture: pass with no reference declared (mechanism off), pass against an approved reference, fail on a one-byte change; on Jade & Ember the regression result is identical before and after.

components.name: Build integrity checks
components.summary: Determinism (two builds equal), delivery (self-contained, no tooling), asset manifest and content-hashed copy. Portability: the delivered folder works from an extracted ZIP, file://, a domain root, a subdirectory, pretty URLs and without byte-range support.

redesign.notes: assets.mjs compares the hashed copy with v0.8 in the browser (baseline optional); file lists and the recorded assets.manifest.json path come from the manifest.

components.verify: Fixture determinism and delivery cases (mutation tests); Jade & Ember tree hash unchanged.

components.name: Configuration validation and component contracts
components.summary: Validates configuration against JSON Schemas before the build; renders every component against contracts; the configuration loader.

redesign.notes: client.schema.json carries the restaurant business block (address, hours, ordering); the base client schema (identity, flags, seo, contact) stays in the core and the industry block moves to the adapter. The loader assumes four named files (client, site, copy, menu).

components.verify: Schema accepts the fixture and Jade & Ember configuration; every forbidden combination (demo flag with indexing, structured data with noindex, demonstration wording in an indexable build) is refused with a message.

components.name: Restaurant industry adapter
components.summary: Restaurant-shaped components (dish, menu category, hours, owner note, steps), the menu page renderer, the copy and menu schemas and the component contracts they satisfy.

redesign.notes: Stays with restaurant projects. Also receives, from FM-15, the Restaurant JSON-LD (jsonLdFor, validateRestaurant, hoursSpecs) and the BUSINESS fixtures. Master spec 02 names the industry value site_type.restaurant_hospitality; the adapter id should align with it.

components.verify: The adapter passes its own contract tests on the fixture restaurant; a non-restaurant project loads the core without the adapter present.

components.name: Accessibility and interaction checks
components.summary: Keyboard order and focus, 320 px reflow and zoom, forced colours, accessibility-tree rules, DOM order against reading order.

redesign.notes: Selectors (.nav-toggle, .skip/.jump), the Pause-control wording and the five-page walk come from the manifest selector map and page registry.

components.verify: Mutation tests on the fixture (a removed skip link, a keyboard trap, a clipped target) fail for the right reason in three engines; Jade & Ember results identical.

components.name: Key contact-link check
components.summary: Every telephone link at nine mobile widths: readable, inside the viewport, operable.

redesign.notes: Generic in principle (key contact links: phone, email, map, order) but selectors and expectations are restaurant-shaped; owner decision F-G4-01 is specific to Jade & Ember's appearance.

components.verify: Fixture with phone, email and map links at nine widths; Jade & Ember unchanged.

components.name: Jade & Ember site-specific verification
components.summary: The approved WebKit text-spacing correction check, engine feature records, and the behaviour scenarios keyed to this site's pages and controls.
components.target: stays in Jade & Ember (as a project check registered through the manifest)

redesign.notes: Not reusable: APR-JE-029 / F-G5-04 and scenario code for this site. It demonstrates the project-check extension point the core must offer.

components.verify: Registered through the manifest and still run by the core runner; results identical.

components.name: Security policy engine, CSP and privacy
components.summary: Builds the Content Security Policy and headers from one policy and proves them in three engines; privacy (no storage, cookies, third parties); the style-attribute hash behaviour (D-11).

redesign.notes: security.mjs also renders the host files (_headers, nginx, Apache) which belong to the hosting adapters (FM-22); HSTS includeSubDomains default is a known deviation (D-P3-4, D-P4-5); d11 names this site's photograph selectors; noindex headers are keyed to the demonstration channel; defaults (framework) versus tighten-only project overrides (master spec 13).

components.verify: CSP generated for fixture and Jade & Ember, identical to today for Jade & Ember; header renderers tested per adapter; HSTS default has no includeSubDomains.

components.name: Dependency, secrets and CI policy checks
components.summary: Dependency pinning, lockfile integrity, licences and advisories; credentials in tree and history; the GitHub Actions workflow policy.

redesign.notes: check:ci encodes Jade-specific rules (push only to the v0.9 development branch, main forbidden, schedule/workflow_run/release triggers forbidden, only two named actions, must run npm run verify, full fetch for the baseline) and rejects a reusable-workflow uses:. Measured: the cinematic template's workflow fails 12 of its rules, one of them a false positive (the word claude in a branch name). Needs a profile-driven policy, SHA-pinned reusable workflows, an exception register with expiry (D-P6-7), SBOM and provenance checks (D-P6-5).

components.verify: Fixture workflows (compliant and each violation) judged correctly; template workflow judged with only true findings; advisory exception expiry fails closed.

components.name: Search and AI-discovery generators and validators
components.summary: Canonical URLs, sitemap, robots.txt, llms.txt, crawler classes and review record, structured-data checks, reserved-host test, internal-link and HTML validation.

redesign.notes: Engineering imports project source (seven imports of src/lib/seo.mjs, crawlers.mjs and config.mjs): the generators move into the framework so any builder can call them. Restaurant JSON-LD moves to FM-09; the framework selects a schema type per industry (D-P4-2), supports an approved social image (D-P4-3), evaluates DuckAssistBot and Meta-ExternalFetcher (D-P4-1). isReservedHost is a denylist (12 of 27 sample provider hosts unrecognised): production-domain authorisation becomes positive (priority 4).

components.verify: Fixture indexable build generates and validates all artifacts; Jade & Ember artifacts byte-identical; domain authorisation scenarios in the dry run.

components.name: External-link verification
components.summary: Registry of external destinations, a classified verifier (verified, blocked, unavailable, inconclusive, insecure), an append-only history, an informational CI job.

redesign.notes: Becomes a client-production release requirement bound to the registry digest (D-P5-1, finding RG-02). The Jade credit link correction (D-P5-3) is site content.

components.verify: Scripted-network cases (already 36); the release requirement scenarios in the dry run.

components.name: Media inspection and rights
components.summary: Media format, dimension, alt-text, flashing, reduced-motion and Pause checks; the rights inventory with a WOFF2 name-table reader and licence-section comparison.

redesign.notes: The rights approval must bind to the exact asset inventory digest (D-P5-4, RG-03); provider-terms evidence stays open (D-P5-5); asset status vocabulary should map to the master Asset Manifest states (ready, remediation_required, blocked) in spec 03.

components.verify: Inventory scenarios (missing, unverified, wrong digest, negated row) fail; Jade & Ember inventory result unchanged.

components.name: Release gate, manifest and approvals
components.summary: The release policy per channel, the gate, the release manifest and its schema, the approvals parser, the release tool (gate, manifest, prepare, search-digest).

redesign.notes: The centre of the Gate 6 priorities: approvals and CI evidence bound to an immutable candidate artifact digest (RG-01); structured approval records with explicit statuses, reviewer authorisation and revocation (RG-04..RG-07); authentic verification evidence (RG-08); positive production-domain authorisation; a restricted demonstration channel that cannot masquerade (RG-13); attestation or signing evaluated before the architecture is final (RG-14); the previously approved requirements added (RG-02, RG-03, RG-09..RG-12).

components.verify: All 112 dry-run scenarios retained and extended; every RG finding becomes a scenario that blocks; manifest deterministic and valid under two validators.

components.name: Human-evidence tooling
components.summary: Evidence specification, validator, scaffolds, generated tester procedures, the evidence classes E1/E2/E3.

redesign.notes: Records live in the repository and name the commit (RG-01); the attestation is self-declared text (authenticity, priority 3); the page list and device list are Jade-specific data inside the spec.

components.verify: Evidence validator cases (122 today) retained; records bind to the candidate artifact digest; forged or reused records rejected.

components.name: Release dry run and package verifier
components.summary: Runs the real release tool against a synthetic client build in a throwaway copy; verifies a prepared package from its own bytes; 112 scenarios and 12 measured probes.

redesign.notes: Retained as a blocking check (priority 8). The sandbox copies the Jade project and the scenarios name Jade files; it moves to the generic fixture and is extended with every RG finding and every Gate 6 requirement.

components.verify: Dry run on the generic fixture and on Jade & Ember; each new requirement has a blocking scenario; probes shrink as gaps close.

components.name: Self-test suites and fixtures
components.summary: Mutation and targeted negative tests for every check (Gate 1 to Gate 5), the client fixture and the in-memory evidence fixtures.

redesign.notes: About 1,090 lines of self-tests damage copies of Jade & Ember files; client-fixture.mjs holds the restaurant demonstration-to-client text edits. They must run on a generic fixture site so the core proves itself, with Jade & Ember as the reference consumer.

components.verify: Every existing negative case has an equivalent on the generic fixture; counts reconciled (251, 122, 25 and the Gate 1 to 3 cases).

components.name: Hosting adapters and requirements
components.summary: Host-file generation, the static-folder hosting check (Cloudflare Pages limits), hosting assessment documents, adapter interface, Vercel specification, live verification checklist.

redesign.notes: Adapters implement one interface (HOSTING-ADAPTER-INTERFACE.md): header rendering, URL style, 404 behaviour, cache rules, bundle manifest. Requirements to carry: a real 404 (D-P3-1), domain-root base URL (D-P3-2), staged-bundle verification (D-P3-3), HSTS opt-in (D-P3-4), provider documentation re-verified (D-P3-6). Live verification needs a separately authorised preview (D-P3-5).

components.verify: Adapter golden outputs for the fixture; the same delivered folder passes check:portability under both adapters; live checklist items recorded only when performed.

components.name: CI workflow and CI documentation
components.summary: The seven-job GitHub Actions workflow and the document that specifies the runner.
components.target: framework repo: .github/workflows/ (reusable workflows) plus a thin caller in each client repository

redesign.notes: Becomes SHA-pinned reusable workflows (workflow_call) in the framework repository, called from a short workflow in each client repository; Node 24 and verified Action versions (D-P6-2, D-P6-3). The hard-coded Jade branch, job names and Node pin become inputs.

components.verify: A client repository that only contains the caller workflow and the manifest runs the same checks; workflow policy check passes on caller and on the reusable workflow.

components.name: Creative-authority pin check
components.summary: Records and verifies the design authority (skill path and SHA-256, licence) and the framework reference; reads, never modifies, the framework.

redesign.notes: Generalised to a per-project creative-authority pin in the manifest; the framework Release (spec 14) does not exist yet (authority.json release is null), so the pin is a commit.

components.verify: Fixture with a correct pin passes, a wrong hash or missing skill fails; Jade & Ember unchanged.

components.name: Design tokens structure check
components.summary: The shared custom properties in styles.css as engineering structure (defined, used, contrast pairs), against a frozen snapshot.

redesign.notes: Compares with the frozen v0.8 values (a project fact); the reusable part checks structure and contrast pairs only and must never choose values (see the creative-authority boundary).

components.verify: Fixture tokens structure cases; Jade & Ember snapshot comparison stays as a project check.

components.name: Performance budgets
components.summary: Page-weight budgets with growth against a reference and Core Web Vitals under throttling.

redesign.notes: budgets.json holds measured Jade values; the framework carries tier defaults (master spec 13 refers to versioned CORE performance policy) and a project may only tighten.

components.verify: Budget cases on the fixture; Jade & Ember budgets and results unchanged.

components.name: Jade & Ember project records and policy data
components.summary: Owner-approved records and data files that describe this project, not the mechanism: authority, baseline, allowlists, findings, recorded asset manifest, tokens snapshot, media rights inventory, external destinations and verification history, crawler review, secrets allowlist.

redesign.notes: These are facts and decisions of one project. Their shapes (schemas) are reusable and belong with their mechanisms; the contents never move. Under the Gate 6 model, approval and evidence records leave the tracked tree or are bound to the artifact digest (RG-01).

components.verify: Shapes validated by the framework schemas; the contents unchanged.

components.name: Jade & Ember website (delivered site and renderer)
components.summary: Configuration, page and shared renderers, the five delivered pages, styles, scripts, fonts, media, version and package files.

redesign.notes: The approved visual design and its renderer are frozen (v0.8 baseline). Whether a shared static renderer (build.mjs plus generic components) becomes a framework component is an owner decision, not part of the engineering extraction: the engineering verifies the delivered folder, whichever builder produced it.

components.verify: Delivered folder byte-identical before and after every Gate 6 package (tree hash 9061a227…).

components.name: Legacy tests and development tools
components.summary: Older axe, contrast and extracted-folder suites, the latency probe, the Gate 5 diagnostic, video QA, the local server, the Lighthouse configuration.
components.target: engineering/tooling/ (kept as optional tools) or stays

redesign.notes: Lighthouse CI is replaced by a tested direct Lighthouse run before client production (D-P6-1); the other tools are optional diagnostics and need no extraction for Gate 6.

components.verify: Direct Lighthouse reproduces the current thresholds (performance 0.8 warn, accessibility 0.95 error, best practices 0.9 warn, SEO 0.6 warn, three runs, median).

components.name: Engineering documentation (becomes the framework specification)
components.summary: Engineering README, security, hosting-by-mode and search-readiness documents, and the security and dependency-maintenance policy proposal.

redesign.notes: Rewritten as framework documentation with the project names removed; the policy proposal already separates mechanism from fact (its section 3).

components.verify: Every statement traces to a check or a requirement id; reviewed by someone other than the author.

components.name: Jade & Ember governance and history documents
components.summary: Approvals log, build brief, ledger, framework reference, plans, phase reports, QA record, media rights policy and proposal, dependency advisory register.
components.target: stays in Jade & Ember (generic passages feed FM-30)

redesign.notes: Project history and decisions. The approvals log is the human record; its Markdown-table form is replaced by structured records (priority 2) with the table kept as a rendering.

components.verify: Unchanged; cross-references updated when files move.

components.name: Phase evidence artefacts
components.summary: Screenshots, diagnostics and the hero-video gate record kept as evidence for earlier decisions.

redesign.notes: Evidence for decisions about this project's appearance and media.

components.verify: Hashes unchanged.

components.name: Showcase repository root and frozen baseline data
components.summary: The STS Cinematic Showcase hub page and README, and the frozen v0.8 baseline checksums and preview package.

redesign.notes: Repository-level files of the showcase, not of the engineering. The baseline data is a frozen record.

components.verify: Unchanged; check:baseline still passes.

components.name: Gate 5 assessment and closure artefacts
components.summary: The Phase 8 assessment (matrix data, its checker and generator, the reports) and the Phase 9 closure (closure ledger, verifier, closure report, Gate 6 readiness summary).
components.target: stays (absorbed by the framework specification at G6-0)
components.verify: check:framework-matrix passes (every file classified, every reference valid, generated Markdown current).

workPackages.title: Decisions and specification
workPackages.summary: Close the Phase 8 owner decisions; write the engineering framework specification (proposed architecture/16) and the project manifest schema; define what a Framework Release is for engineering and how projects consume it (pinned commit, not a package); decide builder scope. Documents only. Any change to the framework repository needs the owner's explicit approval first. It also records, as owner decisions, the builder-scope ruling (deterministic static generation is permitted, Lovable is an optional builder; engineering verifies any builder's folder), the relation of the Essential, Premium and Cinematic offerings to the framework tiers with a single base engineering (OI-2), how the architecture's visual packages sit under the sole creative authority (OI-1), the reviewer evidence bundle an independent reviewer receives so that every verification is reproducible without the implementer (OI-7), and the framework README and numbering fixes (OI-5).
workPackages.verification: Specification reviewed by someone other than its author; every statement traces to a check or a requirement id; the manifest schema validates Jade & Ember's manifest (written by hand, not yet used).

workPackages.title: Runtime and tooling hygiene
workPackages.summary: Node 24 baseline verified against the full suite; Node 24-compatible pinned Actions; the direct Lighthouse runner replacing @lhci/cli; the parse-cache-control licence evidence. Small, independent, and done early because every later verification runs on this runtime.
workPackages.verification: Full verify and the three engines green on Node 24 with the new pins; Lighthouse thresholds reproduced; npm audit reports 0 advisories in the installed tree; check:ci policy updated and passing.

scope.note: Derived from GATE-6-IMPLEMENTATION-ORDER.md (G6-1) and the owner's seven scope items. The master framework repository, the main branch and the frozen baseline branch are not in scope. Pages, styles, scripts, fonts, media, configuration, the renderer, the CSP and the release policy and gate are denied.

workPackages.title: Release model v2
workPackages.summary: Design (2a) then implement (2b), in Jade & Ember as the reference consumer: a candidate artifact digest that excludes approvals; separately recorded approvals and CI evidence; structured approval records with statuses, reviewer authorisation and revocation; complete and authentic verification evidence bound to the digest; positive production-domain authorisation; a restricted demonstration channel; and the attestation or signing evaluation completed before the architecture is final. The 112-scenario dry run stays blocking and is extended with one scenario per finding RG-01 to RG-14.
workPackages.verification: Every RG finding has a blocking scenario; the committed-ledger flow reaches green; a forged verification report, a rejected or revoked approval and a masquerading demonstration are refused; dry run stays blocking in CI.

workPackages.title: Requirement completion
workPackages.summary: Add the previously approved requirements to the gate: external links (D-P5-1), media rights bound to the asset inventory digest (D-P5-4) with provider-terms evidence (D-P5-5), dependency and security requirements incl. SBOM, provenance, exception expiry (D-P6-5, D-P6-7), crawler evaluation (D-P4-1), approved social image support (D-P4-3). The credit-link and Noto notice corrections need their own authorisation because they change delivered files.
workPackages.verification: One blocking dry-run scenario per requirement; probes RG-02, RG-03, RG-10 and RG-11 close; delivered folder unchanged except the two separately authorised corrections.

workPackages.title: Hosting adapters and hosting requirements
workPackages.summary: One adapter interface; Cloudflare Pages first, then Vercel and a plain static adapter; a real 404 (D-P3-1), domain-root base URLs (D-P3-2), staged-bundle manifest and deployed-bytes comparison (D-P3-3), HSTS opt-in (D-P3-4, D-P4-5). Provider documentation must be re-verified by a person before an adapter is built (D-P3-6). Live verification needs a separately authorised preview (D-P3-5). MONOLITH House & Design (proof of concept #2) targets Vercel, so the Vercel adapter and its re-verified provider documentation must be complete before that project starts; any Vercel preview needs its own authorisation (D-P3-5).
workPackages.verification: Golden outputs per adapter; the same delivered folder passes check:portability under both; RG-12 closes; live checklist items recorded only when performed.

workPackages.title: De-coupling refactor in Jade & Ember
workPackages.summary: Project manifest, core/adapter split, generic fixture site, project-check extension point, with a parity proof: 38+ checks, byte-identical delivered output, identical reports, dry run unchanged. No move of files to the framework yet.
workPackages.verification: Parity: delivered tree hash 9061a227…, reports identical, 100% of the dry-run scenarios, the self-test case counts reconciled to the generic fixture.

workPackages.title: Extraction into the framework repository
workPackages.summary: Add the de-coupled core, adapters and fixtures to the master framework repository, which owns the reusable engineering (D-P8-1), on a branch (never main), with framework CI running the generic fixture. Needs the owner's explicit approval to modify the framework repository, which has not been given.
workPackages.verification: Framework CI green on the generic fixture in three engines; independent review; Jade & Ember untouched.

workPackages.title: Centralised GitHub automation
workPackages.summary: SHA-pinned reusable workflows in the framework repository called from a short workflow in each client repository; per-repository Dependabot configuration generated from a template with human approval and no automatic merging (D-P6-4); scheduled supply-chain, external-link and read-only live-site checks run from GitHub-hosted runners. Nothing is installed on a client's hosting; the client repository holds only a caller workflow and the manifest. The current workflow policy forbids schedule triggers and reusable-workflow calls and must be changed deliberately. GitHub Actions is the foundation for centralised maintenance and security (D-P8-8); no software is installed on any client host.
workPackages.verification: A scratch repository with only the caller workflow and manifest runs the checks; the policy check passes on caller and reusable workflows; update PRs never merge themselves.

workPackages.title: Consumption and independent validation
workPackages.summary: Jade & Ember consumes the framework at a pinned Git revision (M4, D-P8-2); the framework is validated independently by the ladder V1 to V4 (generic fixture, reference consumer parity, a second structure, mutation tests) with ChatGPT reviewing evidence and architecture (D-P8-10); a readiness checklist is completed. Then MONOLITH House & Design, the established proof of concept #2 (a fictional five-page luxury residential architecture/design-build website targeted for Vercel), begins; being fictional it uses the demonstration channel, not client production.
workPackages.verification: All four validation levels recorded; readiness checklist signed by the owner; no engine check silently skipped.

priorities.text: Design a release model bound to an immutable candidate artifact digest, with separately recorded approvals and CI evidence.
Replace keyword-based approval interpretation with structured records, explicit statuses, reviewer authorization and revocation handling.
Require complete, authentic verification evidence associated with the candidate artifact.
Address the previously approved external-link, media-rights, dependency/security and hosting requirements.
Evaluate package attestation or signing before finalizing the release architecture.
Preserve a restricted demonstration channel without permitting it to masquerade as client production.
Retain the blocking release dry run.
